- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility.
- After a price spike (forecast > 82), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions at 5% of prior peak to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 78), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the window (first 5–7 days); apply 1–3% downward bias to first 5 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3-day trend to anchor forecast.
